messages.subject: confounding problem of interaction terms
parts:
Dear all,

I had a look at the paper "Age-space-time CAR models in Bayesian disease mapping" by Goicoa, Ugarte et.al..

Therein they built the following model for mortality rates:


with \beta the intercept \phi_i a spatial Leroux random effect, \delta_j a age random effect (RW1) and \gamma_t a temporal random effect (RW1). The \eta`s are interaction terms of Type IV (space-age, space-time and age-time effects) with 
covariance matrices given by the Kronecker product of the marginal covariances.

I would like to modify this model for mortality rates, by adding age as a fixed effect (factor) instead of a RW1 model, omitting the temporal random effect (RW1) and ending up with a spatial Leroux random effect and the three interaction effects, i.e., 

log r=\beta+ factor(age) +\phi_i+\eta^1+\eta^2+\eta^3.

Do you think this is still an identifiable/plausible/legit model? Because in Knorr-Held (2000) it is written that: 
In general, however, we recommend omitting only those main effects that are not assumed to interact.

I wonder because for me it seems more interpretable if I add factor(age) instead of a RW(1) on age. Since a fixed effect tells me how much more certain age groups are affect by mortality than others. How would you interpret a RW1 model on age?

I am very much looking forward to your answer and already say thanks in advance.

Best,
Corinna
